24.0.0.en: The earth is the LORD'S, and the fulness thereof; the world, and they that dwell therein.

24.0.1.en: 1- He declares that God is the Creator of the earth and all the creatures on it, and therefore He has authority over all mankind. It is natural that they should worship Him. But whoever turns away from Him and worships idols is a strange person in his thinking, because there is no creator but God; how then can a person leave his Creator?

24.0.2.en: 2- This verse comforts the Jews who were captive far from Jerusalem and Judea: the whole earth belongs to God, and not only Jerusalem and its surroundings; therefore the captives can lift up their prayers to God from the captivity.

24.0.3.en: 3- This verse is a prophecy about the Church of the New Testament, where people from all the regions of the earth and from various places believe in Christ.

24.0.4.en: 4- Every person imprisoned in a jail, or exiled, or facing any tribulation or injustice, is comforted that his God owns the whole earth, so he is encouraged and prays, confident in the power of his God, who rescues him, protects him and satisfies him, as happened with Jeremiah while he was in prison, when God called him to stand and pray and be comforted (Jer 33:3).

24.1.0.en: For he hath founded it upon the seas, and established it upon the rivers.

24.1.1.en: 1- God founded the earth upon the seas and the rivers, which signify trials. He founded it strong, such that trials cannot prevail against it as long as it holds fast to Him. And He does not let trials be beyond a person's strength, and He makes with them the way of escape.

24.1.2.en: 2- The seas and rivers also signify the Holy Spirit and the Holy Sacraments, especially the sacrament of Baptism; and God founded His Church on the Holy Sacraments and the work of the Holy Spirit, and gave those who believe in Him the ability to live in His house, whose characteristics will appear in the following verses.

24.1.3.en: 3- Rivers water and moisten the earth and make it able to grow crops, and help creatures to live by drinking from them. That is, God takes care of the needs of men, His children, and puts in the seas and rivers the fish from which man benefits.

24.1.4.en: 4- God founded the earth upon the seas, and it is a miraculous work that it should be firm upon the moving seas and rivers; and therefore God's children are assured that they are firm in Him, however the affairs of life around them may change.

24.1.5.en: 5- The rivers signify the disciples, the Apostles and the priests, the servants of the New Testament, who convey the work of the Holy Spirit to the believers, so that their souls are watered and satisfied and live with God powerfully.

24.1.6.en: Be at ease throughout your life, because you are in a faithful hand, the hand of God, the Almighty and Creator of all, and do not be troubled by tribulations, because they are by His permission for the growth of your life and your being approved before Him. Hold fast to your faith and your prayers, and you will pass successfully through all tribulations.

24.2.s.en: (2) The conditions for entering the house of the Lord

24.2.0.en: Who shall ascend into the hill of the LORD? and who shall stand in his holy place?

24.2.1.en: 1- The hill of the Lord is the one on which God's Temple was built in Jerusalem, and what is meant is: who deserves to offer worship acceptable before God? And the holy place is the Temple.

24.2.2.en: 2- The holy place is the Church of the New Testament, and the hill is Christ, the head of the body. And what is meant is: what are the necessary qualities of the one who ascends the hill and stands in the holy place?

24.2.3.en: 3- The one who has received the sacrament of Baptism, as we mentioned in (v. 2), is the one able, by the new nature, to ascend the hill and stand in the holy place, that is, to stand in the Church and partake of the Holy Sacraments. And standing also means steadfastness, that is, to be a firm pillar in the house of the Lord.

24.2.4.en: 4- Ascending is from earthly things to heavenly things, and the hill represents steadfastness, that is, he grows in steadfastness in Christ. And the process of ascending is continuous, because Christ the hill has no end. And it is not possible to ascend to the fullness of the stature of Christ, that is, upon the hill, except with the help of grace.

24.3.0.en: He that hath clean hands, and a pure heart; who hath not lifted up his soul unto vanity, nor sworn deceitfully.

24.3.1.en: 1- The first condition for entering the house of the Lord is cleanness of hands, that is, having pure, clean works, which have no purpose except pleasing God and the salvation of the souls of others.

24.3.2.en: 2- The second condition is purity of heart; for works to be clean, the intention of the heart must be pure, otherwise the works become superficial, for show, to please people and not God.

24.3.3.en: 3- The third condition is keeping away from everything that is vain, such as the gatherings of the world and its works, however prevalent they may be. As long as they do not please God and do not lead to the salvation of the soul, they are vain.

24.3.4.en: 4- The fourth condition is that a person's will be good, so that he lifts up his soul to good things and not to vanity. And according to how strong his spiritual will is, he will grow in the knowledge of God and his relationship with Him.

24.3.5.en: 5- The fifth condition is truthfulness and faithfulness in dealing with others. In the Old Testament he swears truthfully, or in the New Testament he is truthful in his promises. But whoever swears or promises with deceit and lying is a son of the devil, the liar and the father of lies, even if he has an appearance of piety and a position in the Church, or even in her service. And whoever seeks the truth and rejects vanity from his heart will of course be faithful in his dealings with others, and will not deceive anyone or lie to him.

24.4.0.en: He shall receive the blessing from the LORD, and righteousness from the God of his salvation.

24.4.1.en: 1- The one who has the preceding qualities receives a blessing from the Lord. What is meant by the blessing is all the divine gifts, spiritual, psychological and material, so he is in spiritual fullness and in need of nothing material, because God arranges his needs.

24.4.2.en: 2- The one who has these conditions also receives righteousness, that is, a pure life and mercy through the forgiveness of his sins, the finding of excuses for him, and support in his spiritual and material striving, so he is successful in all that his hands undertake, as the first Psalm says, "whatsoever he doeth shall prosper" (Ps 1:3); and besides the blessing and righteousness he receives divine salvation, so he lives the life of salvation, far from sin and enjoying fellowship with Christ, in preparation for his departure to the Kingdom of Heaven.

24.4.3.en: 3- The One who receives all the blessings and all the righteousness is Christ, God incarnate. And at the same time He is the source of the blessings and mercy that He poured out on those who believe in Him by His Incarnation; He alone is without sin, as He said to the Jews, "Which of you convinceth me of sin?" (Jn 8:46).

24.4.4.en: 4- Whoever ascends to the hill of the Lord receives blessings; he is poor and has nothing to give, but his striving toward the house of the Lord and his seeking God give him countless blessings, and he receives Christ Himself through His most holy Body and Blood, and He dwells in his heart for ever.

24.5.0.en: This is the generation of them that seek him, that seek thy face, O Jacob. Selah.

24.5.1.en: 1- Whoever holds fast to the preceding conditions seeks the face of Jacob, or the face of the God of Jacob as in the Septuagint translation; for what is meant is that just as Jacob saw God, so whoever seeks the Lord wants to enjoy seeing the face of God. Although this is impossible for man because of the loftiness of God, God in His humility showed Himself to Moses, and to everyone who strives toward Him and loves Him, like all the saints in the New Testament.

24.5.2.en: 2- Those who seek the face of Jacob are those who walk as Jacob walked in the way of perfection (Gen 25:27).

24.5.3.en: 3- As Jacob received the blessing of the birthright, so everyone who ascends to the hill of the Lord and seeks Him receives the blessings that Christ, the firstborn among many brethren, grants him, so he receives the blessings of salvation in the New Testament in the Church.

24.5.4.en: 4- The one who seeks the face of God means that he longs and strives, that is, struggles; he is not content with the inner desire but supports it with spiritual striving.

24.5.5.en: 5- At the end of this verse we find the word Selah, which is a musical pause; that is, the preceding verses speak about those prepared to enter the house of the Lord, while the following verses tell us about Christ the victorious, glorified King.

24.5.6.en: God loves you and sought you by His Incarnation, and still seeks you every day; therefore He rejoices greatly in your striving toward Him in response to His love. Your striving in all the spiritual practices, even if with compulsion, is very precious to God.

24.6.0.en: Lift up your heads, O ye gates; and be ye lift up, ye everlasting doors; and the King of glory shall come in. Gates: the portals and entrances.

24.6.1.en: 1- The angels who witnessed the Incarnation of Christ and ministered to Him on earth (Mt 4:11) knew that He is God; therefore they ascended with the spirit of Christ so that He might enter heaven, and called to the angels who guard the gates of Paradise, or the Kingdom, to lift up and open these gates so that Christ, the King of glory, may enter.

24.6.2.en: 2- Christ does not need the gates to be opened for Him, because He is God, who fills every place, and no one hinders Him, but He speaks as a man, because He is the firstborn among many brethren. He represents the new humanity ascending to enter Paradise and the Kingdom; therefore it was necessary to announce to the angels standing at the gates of Paradise and the Kingdom that a human being would enter, namely Christ, God incarnate.

24.6.3.en: 3- He says "lift up" and not "open", because Christ by His Incarnation bowed the heavens and came down, so when He ascends the gates are lifted up.

24.6.4.en: 4- These everlasting doors are, of course, not the doors of the Temple of Jerusalem nor the temple of the Church of the New Testament, but they are everlasting doors that were closed from of old, from the days of Adam when he was driven out of Paradise, and now they are opened that Christ may enter. The everlasting doors mean that they are not material doors, and also that they are from a long time ago, that is, from everlasting.

24.6.5.en: 5- These gates signify the gates of the heart of man and the gates of his senses, which should be lifted up to heavenly things, so that Christ may enter into them and dwell, and man may enjoy His work in him. And He says "lift up your heads", meaning that human beings should lift their heads toward heaven to behold God, that is, love prayer, praise and contemplation.

24.6.6.en: 6- He says gates and doors, and not a single door, to declare that there are many heavens, or degrees in heaven, which human beings enter according to their striving and the work of grace in them. Christ, God incarnate, enters all these and opens them, so that all who believe in Him may enter after Him, each according to his degree.

24.7.0.en: Who is this King of glory? The LORD strong and mighty, the LORD mighty in battle.

24.7.1.en: 1- The angels who guard the gates of heaven asked, saying: Who is the King of glory? For they are sure that it is forbidden for any human being to enter Paradise since it was closed in the days of Adam; so who, then, is this King of glory?!

24.7.2.en: 2- The angels ascending with the spirit of Christ answered them and declared to them that the King of glory is not merely a man, but is the mighty Lord, God become man, and they of course know God, so they opened the gates at once.

24.7.3.en: 3- The mighty Lord is Christ our God, who by His might bound Satan on the Cross, so that he no longer has authority over God's children to take them to Hades; rather, by Christ's opening of Paradise as a victorious bearer of good news He gives a chance to all human beings who believe in Him to enter heaven, which had been closed before them.

24.7.4.en: 4- What the angels ascending with the spirit of Christ said, that is, "the Lord mighty in battle", is the same expression with which Moses began his song after crossing the Red Sea (Ex 15:3), which was a type of what Christ would do in the fullness of time, by His victory over Satan and his binding on the Cross, which the angels ascending with the spirit of Christ announced to heaven.

24.8.0.en: Lift up your heads, O ye gates; even lift them up, ye everlasting doors; and the King of glory shall come in.

24.8.1.en: 1- He repeats here what he said in (v. 7); so what is the reason? Did the angels who guard the gates of heaven not understand? Of course not. They certainly understood that this is Christ, the mighty Lord. But he repeats the same words here because the angels ascending with the spirit of Christ rose to another, higher heaven and asked the angels who guard these second gates to lift them up. Perhaps the first heaven is meant to be the Paradise of Joy, and the second heaven the Kingdom of Heaven.

24.8.2.en: 2- We should not be surprised if some angels know that this is the spirit of Christ and others do not. There is understanding among the angels, and different abilities, as we see in (Dan 10:12-14), where we find that Gabriel was speaking with Daniel, and likewise the angel appointed over Persia, but Satan, referred to as the prince of Persia, stood before Daniel to hinder him from his service, and there the archangel Michael intervened and drove Satan away from Daniel's way.

24.8.3.en: 3- The angels mentioned as guards of the gates do not include archangels, such as Michael and Gabriel, because these had knowledge of the Incarnation of Christ; for Gabriel is the one who gave the good news to the Virgin, and Michael is the one who announced the Resurrection and sat on the stone after it was rolled away. The meaning of this is that there was a group of angels, such as the archangels, who knew about the matter of redemption, but they were not proud of their knowledge, and the angels who did not know this matter were not grieved. Rather, all were in joy at receiving the ascending Christ.

24.9.0.en: Who is this King of glory? The LORD of hosts, he is the King of glory. Selah.

24.9.1.en: 1- For the first time in the Old Testament the expression "Lord of hosts", that is, Lord of the armies, or Lord Sabaoth, is used; it is an expression particular to the Father, but the Son is described by it here because of His victory over Satan and his binding.

24.9.2.en: 2- The expression "Lord of hosts" or "Lord of the armies" is mentioned because Christ by His authority, after His victory over Satan, reigns over the hearts of His children and gives them a place with Him in Paradise, and then afterward in the Kingdom.

24.9.3.en: God wants to reign over your heart; He completed redemption and died on the Cross for one purpose, which is to free you from your sins and give you a place with Him in heaven. So do not be troubled because of your weakness and your falls, but rise quickly, repent, and ask for His help, and He will free you from sin, even if you fall dozens of times every day.

24.9.4.en: The school of prayer. Of David. "Unto thee, O LORD, do I lift up my soul" (v. 1). Introduction:

24.9.5.en: 1- Its writer is David the prophet.

24.9.7.en: Because of David's suffering from the pursuit of Saul and Absalom and everyone who wronged him.

24.9.9.en: In his old age, because he mentions the sins of his youth (v. 7).

24.9.11.en: A prayer lifted up before God, containing a clear example of acceptable and complete prayer before God; it is considered a school of prayer from which a person learns how to pray.

24.9.12.en: 5- It contains wise sayings, truths of the faith, and guidance for walking in the way of God; it is one of the wisdom Psalms and shows God as the Teacher of man in all aspects of his life.

24.9.13.en: 6- This Psalm is considered a personal lament, as it expresses the feelings of a person who feels loneliness and the multitude of enemies against him, and his clinging to God his Savior.

24.9.14.en: 7- This Psalm is among nine Psalms written according to the Hebrew alphabet, and these nine Psalms are 9, 10, 25, 34, 37, 111, 112, 119, 145.

24.9.15.en: 8- This Psalm is found in the Agpeya in the prayer of the Prime.
